standard.title: Sentence structures to express and craft ideas
standard.description: analyse and evaluate the effectiveness of particular sentence structures to express and craft ideas
standard.prior_knowledge: Students identify how authors vary sentence structures creatively including deliberate fragments (AC9E9LA05). They have not yet analysed and evaluated the effectiveness of particular sentence structures to express and craft ideas.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse and evaluate the effectiveness of particular sentence structures to express and craft ideas.

nodes.label: Identifying deliberate sentence structure choices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify deliberate sentence structure choices in texts — including passive voice, verbless clauses, and sentences beginning with conjunctions — and describe their effect.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one deliberate sentence structure choice (e.g. passive voice, verbless clause) in a provided text and describe its effect.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and describe a range of deliberate sentence structure choices across literary and non-literary texts, explaining how each creates a different effect.
wider: Compare how different authors use the same sentence structure (e.g. passive voice) to different effect across contexts
Examine how sentence structure choices in journalism shape how responsibility is attributed in news reports
Analyse how First Nations Australian authors use sentence structure deliberately to assert voice or perspective in their texts
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires students to evaluate the effectiveness of sentence structures — a judgement that depends on being able to reliably identify and name specific structures. Students who cannot identify the structure cannot evaluate its purposeful use.

response_modes.reason: Recognition of specific sentence structure types (passive voice, verbless clause, conjunction-opening) requires practice across examples before students can reliably identify them in novel texts.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one deliberate sentence structure choice by name or description
Describes the effect the structure creates in the context of the text

nodes.label: Evaluating effectiveness of sentence structures
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate the effectiveness of particular sentence structures in achieving the author’s purpose, making a supported judgement.
nodes.minimum_width: Make a supported judgement about whether a specific sentence structure choice is effective in expressing or crafting an idea in a provided text.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate the effectiveness of a range of sentence structure choices in texts across different purposes and audiences, making reasoned judgements with textual evidence.
wider: Compare the effectiveness of active versus passive constructions in legal, scientific and journalistic texts, evaluating how each serves the text’s purpose
Evaluate how authors’ sentence structure choices shape characterisation or mood in literary texts across different genres
Examine published author interviews or commentary about their sentence-level craft choices and evaluate whether the effects claimed are achieved

response_modes.reason: Evaluation of sentence-level craft requires students to connect micro-level form (the structure) to macro-level effect (purpose, characterisation, persuasion) — this bridging reasoning needs explicit scaffolding.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Sentence structure evaluation is rich across literary, journalistic and legal texts — the contrast between how the same structure functions differently in each context creates genuine analytic depth.
success_criteria: Identifies the sentence structure and its intended effect
Makes a supported judgement about whether the structure is effective for its purpose, with textual evidence
